description:
We are a team participating in the Casablanca Local Event for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We have chosen the "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge because we want to build practical, data-driven solutions to help agriculture adapt to a changing climate.

Why NEX TERRA? We are passionate about using NASA's open data to solve real-world problems. We value quick decision-making, efficient teamwork, and creating a project we are proud to present.

We are ready to build! 🌱🛰️
summary:
NEX TERRA is a web-based decision-support platform that helps Moroccan farmers adapt to climate change through smart crop rotation. Addressing the "Field Shift" challenge, our tool allows farmers to drop a pin on their field and input their priorities (water conservation, soil health, or economic yield).
Our backend integrates directly with the NASA POWER Daily API to fetch real historical climate data including temperature, precipitation, and FAO-56 reference evapotranspiration (ET₀) for the exact farm coordinates. The application then simulates how different crop rotations will perform under future climate scenarios, helping farmers visualize water deficits and soil impacts.
We believe in transparent science. While our economic and resilience metrics are currently illustrative prototype assumptions, the climate data driving our water models is grounded in real NASA observations. NEX TERRA transforms complex Earth observation data into actionable, localized insights, ensuring a resilient agricultural future for Morocco.
details:
NEX TERRA is a web based decision support platform designed to help Moroccan farmers adapt to climate change through smart crop rotation. Addressing the "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge, NEX TERRA transforms complex satellite data into actionable, localized agricultural plans. Our goal is to answer the farmer's most critical question: "What should I grow here, how much water will it need, and what do I do next?"

How It Works

  1. Set Location: The farmer drops a pin on a map of Morocco (covering all 12 administrative regions) or manually enter their exact latitude and longitude coordinates.
  2. Add Farm Details: The user inputs past crops, soil tests, and irrigation access.
  3. Fetch NASA Data: Our backend (FastAPI) dynamically fetches climate data—including temperature, humidity, solar radiation, and precipitation—via the NASA POWER API, along with SMAP, GPM, and MODIS data based on the exact coordinates.
  4. Simulate & Compare: The system applies local crop rules to compare different rotations, calculating water deficits, economic potential, and soil resilience.
  5. Results: The platform displays a comparative plan, highlighting the most suitable crops and irrigation approaches.

Tools & Technologies Used

  • Frontend: React, HTML/CSS, JavaScript (deployed on Vercel).
  • Backend: Python (FastAPI), leveraging data science libraries for the simulation engine.
  • Data Sources: NASA POWER (temperature, ET₀), SMAP (soil moisture), GPM (precipitation), MODIS (EVI/NDVI), and CMIP6 (downscaled climate scenarios). We also integrated Moroccan Ministry of Agriculture data, geoBoundaries, and OpenStreetMap.
  • AI Integration: We utilized AI tools (GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT) to accelerate coding, debugging, and content structuring, as well as to generate and assist with the visual images for the website. This allowed us to focus deeply on the NASA API integration and agricultural modeling.

Creativity & Impact

What makes NEX TERRA unique is our commitment to transparent science. Instead of a "black box" AI, our platform explicitly labels data provenance, known gaps, and limitations directly on the UI (e.g., distinguishing between real NASA climate data and prototype economic assumptions).

Intended Impact:

  • Environmental: Reduces water waste through optimized irrigation planning and protects soil health. (Aligns with SDG 6 and 13).
  • Economic: Lowers farming costs by preventing unnecessary input purchases and optimizing yields. (Aligns with SDG 2).
  • Social: Provides clear, accessible guidance to rural farmers, bridging the gap between complex Earth observation data and daily farming decisions.

Key Factors Considered

Our team prioritized local relevance, focusing exclusively on Morocco's specific climate challenges (water scarcity, irregular rainfall). We also considered data integrity, ensuring our backend includes a robust fallback system so the app remains online during demos, even if the NASA API times out. Finally, we designed the UI to be highly accessible, with future plans to translate it into Darija and Amazigh to serve local farmers directly.
